user_message.content: How can I embed the images directly into the email signature instead of using URLs?

status_update.description: Manus is working on your request

assistant_message.content:
Unfortunately, Outlook's signature editor does not support embedding images as base64 data URIs — that's exactly what caused the "text too long" error earlier, since the base64 strings are enormous.

The standard ways to get images reliably into an Outlook signature are:

| Method | How it works | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Paste from browser** | Open the HTML in a browser, select all, copy, paste into Outlook's editor | Images appear inline and are auto-attached by Outlook | GIFs lose animation; become static |
| **Insert image manually** | In the Outlook signature editor, click the image icon and upload each image file | Images are truly embedded/attached | GIFs lose animation; tedious for multiple images |
| **Hosted URLs (current approach)** | Images load from a CDN link | GIFs animate; tiny file size | Blocked if recipient's client disables external images |
| **Exchange/Microsoft 365 admin** | IT admin deploys org-wide signatures server-side | Most reliable, works for everyone | Requires admin access |

**The most practical recommendation for keeping animated GIFs** is the hosted URL approach you already have. Most modern email clients (Gmail, Outlook, Apple Mail) load external images by default, and recipients can always click "load images" if they don't.

If animation doesn't matter, the easiest path is:
1. Open the lightweight HTML file in your browser
2. Select all → Copy
3. Paste into the Outlook signature editor — Outlook will automatically embed the images as attachments behind the scenes
